question.problem:
$$
[T]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{P}_{C\to B}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $[T]_{C}$ of a linear transformation $T$ with respect to the basis $C$ and the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ shown above. Find the matrix of $T$ relative to the basis $B.$
question.worked_solution:
The connection between the matrices of our linear transformation $T$ relative to the bases $B$ and $C$ is given by the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14157444/assets/2e82c232614bec8a98f079ea56d7913ee13e7b457e33e418198278d2e369fc5c.png)

Here, moving along an arrow means pre-multiplying by the corresponding matrix. Algebraically, we can write this as

$$
[T]_{C}={P}_{C\to B}^{-1}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}.
$$

where ${P}_{C\to B}$ is the change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B.$

Our goal is to compute $[T]_{B}.$ Solving this equation for $[T]_{B},$ we obtain the alternative formulation

$$
[T]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{C}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1}.
$$

First, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{C\to B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B}^{-1} & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-2)\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can compute the matrix of $T$ relative to the basis $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[T]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{C}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 7 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
